events.title: Marie Antoinette Is Guillotined
events.description: Nine months after her husband Louis XVI was executed, the former queen of France was put to death by guillotine in Paris. Her trial and execution came at the height of the French Revolution.
events.significance: Her death marked the end of the Bourbon monarchy's last public symbol and showed how radical the Revolution had become.

events.title: Ether Anesthesia Demonstrated at Massachusetts General Hospital
events.description: Dentist William T. G. Morton publicly demonstrated ether anesthesia during surgery in Boston. The patient was unconscious and the operation went ahead without the usual agony.
events.significance: The demonstration opened the way for modern surgery by making longer and more complex operations possible.

events.title: John Brown Raids Harpers Ferry
events.description: Abolitionist John Brown led a small group of men in an attack on the federal arsenal at Harpers Ferry, Virginia (now West Virginia). The aim was to start an armed uprising against slavery.
events.significance: The raid failed, but it sharply raised tensions between North and South and helped push the United States toward the Civil War.

events.title: The Walt Disney Company Is Founded
events.description: Walt Disney and his brother Roy founded a small animation studio in Los Angeles. It began as the Disney Brothers Cartoon Studio.
events.significance: The studio grew into one of the world's largest entertainment companies and changed animation, film and theme parks.

events.title: Karol Wojtyła Elected Pope John Paul II
events.description: The Archbishop of Kraków was elected pope after a conclave that followed the sudden death of John Paul I. He was the first non-Italian pope in more than 450 years.
events.significance: His long papacy shaped late 20th-century world affairs, including the end of communism in Eastern Europe.
